theorems.name: Two-Element AM-GM Inequality

theorems.name: Exchange Option in the S²-Numéraire (change-of-numéraire instance)
theorems.description: Margrabe's exchange option valued in the second-asset (S²) numéraire is a genuine instance of the general change of numéraire: S²₀·E^{Q^(S²)}[max(S¹/S²−1,0)] = E^Q[max(S¹−S²,0)], where Q^(S²) = numeraireMeasure Q 1 S²_T 1 S²₀. Composes changeOfNumeraire (X = the exchange payoff, N = S²) with the payoff reduction max(S¹−S²,0) = S²·max(S¹/S²−1,0).

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.ExchangeOption

open MeasureTheory MathFin

/-- **The exchange option in the S²-numéraire is a change-of-numéraire instance.** With
the second asset `S²` as numéraire (`numeraireMeasure Q 1 S²_T 1 S²₀`, density
`dQ^(S²)/dQ = S²_T/S²₀`), the option's `S²`-numéraire value equals its value under the
reference measure `Q`:
`S²₀·𝔼^{Q^(S²)}[max(S¹_T/S²_T − 1, 0)] = 𝔼^Q[max(S¹_T − S²_T, 0)]`. This is the general
`changeOfNumeraire` law at `X =` the exchange payoff, `N = S²`, composed with the payoff
reduction `max(S¹−S²,0) = S²·max(S¹/S²−1,0)`; no integrability hypothesis is needed. Re-
exports `MathFin.exchangeOption_numeraire_price`. -/
theorem exchange_option_numeraire_price {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (Q : Measure Ω) (S1T S2T : Ω → ℝ) (S2_0 : ℝ)
    (hS2meas : Measurable S2T) (hS2pos : ∀ ω, 0 < S2T ω) (hS20 : 0 < S2_0) :
    S2_0 * ∫ ω, max (S1T ω / S2T ω - 1) 0
        ∂(MathFin.numeraireMeasure Q (fun _ => 1) S2T 1 S2_0)
      = ∫ ω, max (S1T ω - S2T ω) 0 ∂Q :=
  MathFin.exchangeOption_numeraire_price Q S1T S2T S2_0 hS2meas hS2pos hS20

metadata.reference: Change of numéraire (Geman–El Karoui–Rochet); Margrabe (1978) exchange option in the S²-numéraire
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.exchangeOption_numeraire_price (MathFin/BlackScholes/ExchangeOption.lean): the exchange option's value in the S²-numéraire equals its value under the reference measure Q, as an instance of the general changeOfNumeraire law (Foundations/Numeraire.lean) at X = the exchange payoff, N = S², B ≡ 1, composed with the existing exchange_payoff_eq_ratio. Needs no integrability hypothesis, only strict positivity S²_T > 0. NOTE: ExchangeOption and GarmanNormalForm otherwise contain NO withDensity measure (their numéraire content is payoff algebra / d₁-d₂ closed form), so this is the one genuine measure-level numéraire instance they support — not a fabricated wrapper. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.

theorems.name: Two-Date Geometric-Asian Log-Driver is Gaussian
theorems.description: The geometric-average Asian option's log-driver at two sampling dates s <= t is Gaussian: the average of the Brownian values (B_s + B_t)/2 -- the Gaussian part of log sqrt(S_s * S_t) under GBM -- has the centred Gaussian law N(0, (3s+t)/4), the variance being the covariance sum (s + 2*min(s,t) + t)/4. Turns the geometric average into a priceable lognormal, complementing the AM-GM payoff bound (mf-asian-geom-le-arith-two). The derivation reads the sum of Brownian values as a single Wiener integral of the deterministic step kernel 1/2*(1_{(0,s]} + 1_{(0,t]}) via the new identity int 1_{(0,u]} dB = B_u, so wienerIntegralLp_hasLaw_gaussian gives the Gaussian law and the variance is the kernel L2-norm evaluated through the Brownian covariance int B_s * B_t = min(s,t).

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AsianGeometric

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

/-- **Two-date geometric-Asian log-driver is Gaussian.**
For a Black–Scholes GBM `S_u = S₀·exp((r−σ²/2)u + σ B_u)` sampled at two dates
`s ≤ t`, the geometric average `√(S_s·S_t)` is lognormal because its log-driver —
the average of the Brownian values `(B_s + B_t)/2` — is Gaussian with the
covariance-sum variance `(s + 2·min(s,t) + t)/4 = (3s+t)/4`.
Re-exports `MathFin.asianGeom_driver_hasLaw`. -/
theorem asian_geom_driver_gaussian
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (T : ℝ≥0)
    {s t : ℝ≥0} (hst : s ≤ t) (hsT : s ≤ T) (htT : t ≤ T) :
    HasLaw (fun ω => (B s ω + B t ω) / 2)
      (gaussianReal 0 ((3 * (s : ℝ) + t) / 4).toNNReal) μ :=
  MathFin.asianGeom_driver_hasLaw hB T hst hsT htT

metadata.reference: Geometric-average Asian option; the log geometric average is Gaussian with the Brownian covariance-sum variance
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export from MathFin.BlackScholes.AsianGeometric (asianGeom_driver_hasLaw). The two-date geometric-Asian log-driver (B_s + B_t)/2 has law N(0, (3s+t)/4). Route: (B_s + B_t)/2 = int 1/2*(1_{(0,s]} + 1_{(0,t]}) dB is a single Wiener integral of a deterministic step kernel, using the new foundational identity wienerIntegralLp_stepIndicator (MathFin.Foundations.WienerIntegralIndicator: int 1_{(s,t]} dB = B_t - B_s, from LinearMap.extendOfNorm_eq on the single-basis coefficient); so wienerIntegralLp_hasLaw_gaussian gives the centred Gaussian law, its variance the kernel L2-norm computed on the Omega-side through the Brownian covariance integral_mul_eval (int B_u * B_v = min(u,v)) plus zero-start B_0 = 0 a.s. (from int B_0^2 = 0). Same 'sum of Brownian values as a Wiener integral of a step kernel' route as the Vasicek bond price for the integrated rate; here the kernel is a sum of indicators. Honest scope: two dates (matching the AM-GM entry mf-asian-geom-le-arith-two); the n-date extension is the Finset covariance sum (1/n^2) sum sum min(t_i, t_j), unblocked by the same crux. Axioms-clean: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

theorems.name: n-Date Geometric-Asian Log-Driver is Gaussian
theorems.description: The average of Brownian values (1/n) sum B_{t_i} is Gaussian with variance (1/n^2) sum sum min(t_i,t_j).

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AsianGeometricN

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

/-- **n-date geometric-Asian log-driver is Gaussian.** The average of the Brownian
values `(1/n) ∑ᵢ B_{τᵢ}` — the Gaussian part of the log geometric average of a
Black–Scholes GBM sampled at `τ₁,…,τₙ` — has the centred Gaussian law
`N(0, (1/n²) ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ min(τᵢ,τⱼ))`. Re-exports `MathFin.geomAsianN_driver_hasLaw`. -/
theorem asian_geom_n_driver
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (T : ℝ≥0) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (τ : Fin n → ℝ≥0) (hτT : ∀ i, τ i ≤ T) :
    HasLaw (fun ω => (∑ i, B (τ i) ω) / n)
      (gaussianReal 0 ((∑ i, ∑ j, min (τ i : ℝ) (τ j)) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2).toNNReal) μ :=
  MathFin.geomAsianN_driver_hasLaw hB T hn τ hτT

theorems.name: n-Date Geometric-Asian Call Price (Closed Form)
theorems.description: Discounted geometric-Asian call price equals the Black-Scholes call with effective spot and volatility.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AsianGeometricN

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

/-- **n-date geometric-Asian call price, closed form.** The discounted expected
geometric-Asian call payoff equals the Black–Scholes call price with the effective
spot `Ŝ₀` and volatility `σ_G` — the geometric average reduced to one effective BS
driver. Re-exports `MathFin.geomAsianN_call_price`. -/
theorem asian_geom_n_price
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (T : ℝ≥0) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (τ : Fin n → ℝ≥0) (hτT : ∀ i, τ i ≤ T)
    (S₀ K r σ Tmat : ℝ) (hS₀ : 0 < S₀) (hK : 0 < K) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hTmat : 0 < Tmat)
    (hV : 0 < geomAsianVar τ) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (-r * Tmat) *
        max ((∏ i, (S₀ * Real.exp ((r - σ ^ 2 / 2) * (τ i : ℝ) + σ * B (τ i) ω)) ^ ((n : ℝ)⁻¹))
          - K) 0 ∂μ
      = geomAsianEffSpot S₀ r σ Tmat τ *
          Phi (bsd1 (geomAsianEffSpot S₀ r σ Tmat τ) K r (geomAsianEffVol σ Tmat τ) Tmat)
        - K * Real.exp (-r * Tmat) *
          Phi (bsd2 (geomAsianEffSpot S₀ r σ Tmat τ) K r (geomAsianEffVol σ Tmat τ) Tmat) :=
  MathFin.geomAsianN_call_price hB T hn τ hτT S₀ K r σ Tmat hS₀ hK hσ hTmat hV

theorems.name: Quanto Forward Derived from a Joint-Gaussian FX Model
theorems.description: FX-density-weighted foreign expectation of the terminal equals quantoForward; the -rho sigma_S sigma_FX drift is derived, not posited.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.QuantoGrounding

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- **Girsanov-grounded quanto forward.** The FX-density-weighted foreign expectation of the
foreign terminal equals the quanto-adjusted forward `S₀·exp((r_dom − ρ σ_S σ_FX)T)` — the
`−ρ σ_S σ_FX` drift adjustment is the log-covariance produced by the change of measure, not an
assumption. Re-exports `MathFin.quantoForward_of_gaussian`. -/
theorem quanto_forward_grounded
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (S₀ r_dom σ_S σ_FX ρ T : ℝ) (hT : 0 ≤ T) (hρ : ρ ^ 2 ≤ 1)
    {Z_S Z_perp : Ω → ℝ}
    (hZS : HasLaw Z_S (gaussianReal 0 1) μ) (hZperp : HasLaw Z_perp (gaussianReal 0 1) μ)
    (hZSm : Measurable Z_S) (hZperpm : Measurable Z_perp)
    (hindep : IndepFun Z_S Z_perp μ) :
    ∫ ω, (S₀ * Real.exp ((r_dom - σ_S ^ 2 / 2) * T + σ_S * Real.sqrt T * Z_S ω))
        * Real.exp (-(σ_FX * Real.sqrt T)
            * (ρ * Z_S ω + Real.sqrt (1 - ρ ^ 2) * Z_perp ω) - σ_FX ^ 2 * T / 2) ∂μ
      = quantoForward S₀ r_dom ρ σ_S σ_FX T :=
  MathFin.quantoForward_of_gaussian S₀ r_dom σ_S σ_FX ρ T hT hρ hZS hZperp hZSm hZperpm hindep

theorems.name: Geometric-Asian Closed Form Bounds the Arithmetic Asian Call
theorems.description: In the Black–Scholes model with a Brownian driver, the closed-form n-date geometric-Asian call price (the Black–Scholes call bsV at the geometric average's effective spot and volatility) is at most the discounted expected arithmetic-Asian call payoff of the same GBM sampled at the same dates. No closed form for the arithmetic Asian is claimed.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AsianInequality

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- **The arithmetic Asian call is bounded below by the geometric-Asian closed form.**
Re-exports `MathFin.geomAsianN_bsV_le_arith`. -/
theorem asian_geom_price_le_arith
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (T : ℝ≥0) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (τ : Fin n → ℝ≥0) (hτT : ∀ i, τ i ≤ T)
    (S₀ K r σ Tmat : ℝ) (hS₀ : 0 < S₀) (hK : 0 < K) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hTmat : 0 < Tmat)
    (hV : 0 < geomAsianVar τ) :
    bsV K r (geomAsianEffVol σ Tmat τ) (geomAsianEffSpot S₀ r σ Tmat τ) Tmat ≤
      ∫ ω, Real.exp (-r * Tmat) *
        max ((∑ i, S₀ * Real.exp ((r - σ ^ 2 / 2) * (τ i : ℝ) + σ * B (τ i) ω)) / n - K) 0
        ∂μ :=
  MathFin.geomAsianN_bsV_le_arith hB T hn τ hτT S₀ K r σ Tmat hS₀ hK hσ hTmat hV

theorems.name: Knock-in plus Knock-out Equals the Black–Scholes Call
theorems.description: Under the Black–Scholes lognormal hypothesis, for any measurable barrier-hit event A, the discounted knock-in and knock-out call values (payoff max(S_T − K, 0) on A and on its complement) sum to the Black–Scholes call price bsV. No closed form for either barrier leg is proved.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.BarrierParity

open MeasureTheory
open MathFin

/-- **In–out parity for a Black–Scholes call.** Re-exports
`MathFin.knockIn_add_knockOut_eq_bsV`. -/
theorem knockIn_add_knockOut_bs_call {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {Q : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {S_0 K r σ T : ℝ} {Z : Ω → ℝ} (h : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K r σ T Z)
    {A : Set Ω} (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    knockInValue (Real.exp (-r * T)) Q A (fun ω ↦ max (bsTerminal S_0 r σ T (Z ω) - K) 0) +
        knockOutValue (Real.exp (-r * T)) Q A (fun ω ↦ max (bsTerminal S_0 r σ T (Z ω) - K) 0)
      = bsV K r σ S_0 T :=
  MathFin.knockIn_add_knockOut_eq_bsV h hA

theorems.name: Black–Scholes Call Bounds the Lookback Call from Below

The law of the running maximum is not used; no lookback closed form is claimed.

theorems.name: Basket Moment Matching Is Exact for One Asset
theorems.description: For a one-asset basket (weight 1, forward S·e^{rT}, discount factor e^{−rT}), the moment-matched basket price equals the discounted expected call payoff under the Black–Scholes lognormal hypothesis. For two or more assets the moment-matched price is an approximation and no accuracy statement is made.

theorems.name: First Two Moments of a Lognormal Basket
theorems.description: If each pair of standard-normal drivers (W_i, W_j) is jointly Gaussian with covariance ρ_ij, the basket B_T = Σ w_i F_i exp(σ_i√T·W_i − σ_i²T/2) has mean M₁ = Σ w_i F_i and second moment M₂ = Σ_i Σ_j w_i w_j F_i F_j exp(ρ_ij σ_i σ_j T): the two moments the moment-matching approximation feeds into the Black–Scholes formula. That the matched lognormal prices the basket accurately is not claimed.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.BasketMomentMatching

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin

/-- **The matched moments are the basket's moments.** Combines
`MathFin.integral_basket_eq_basketM1` and `MathFin.integral_basket_sq_eq_basketM2`. -/
theorem basket_lognormal_moments {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {n : ℕ} {W : Fin n → Ω → ℝ} {ρ : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ}
    (hpair : ∀ i j, HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (W i ω, W j ω)) P)
    (hstd : ∀ i, HasLaw (W i) (gaussianReal 0 1) P)
    (hcorr : ∀ i j, cov[W i, W j; P] = ρ i j)
    (w F σ : Fin n → ℝ) {T : ℝ} (hT : 0 ≤ T) :
    ∫ ω, ∑ i, w i * (F i * basketLognormalFactor (σ i) T (W i ω)) ∂P = basketM1 w F ∧
      ∫ ω, (∑ i, w i * (F i * basketLognormalFactor (σ i) T (W i ω))) ^ 2 ∂P
        = basketM2 w F σ ρ T :=
  ⟨MathFin.integral_basket_eq_basketM1 hstd w F σ hT,
    MathFin.integral_basket_sq_eq_basketM2 hpair hstd hcorr w F σ hT⟩

metadata.reference: M. Levy, Pricing European average rate currency options, Journal of International Money and Finance 11(5) (1992) 474–491
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Combines MathFin.integral_basket_eq_basketM1 and MathFin.integral_basket_sq_eq_basketM2 (MathFin/BlackScholes/BasketMomentMatching.lean); the cross-moments come from integral_exp_linear_gaussianPair (MathFin/Foundations/GaussianPairLinearLaw.lean). SCOPE: pairwise joint Gaussianity of the drivers is a hypothesis; the moment-matched price is not compared with the true basket price.

theorems.name: Chooser Option Price in the Black–Scholes Model
theorems.description: With the spot at the chooser date t₁ lognormal and the chooser-date call and put valued at their Black–Scholes prices bsV, bsP of S_{t₁} with remaining maturity T − t₁, the discounted expected chooser payoff e^{−rt₁}·E[max(C_{t₁}, P_{t₁})] equals bsV(K, T) + bsP(K·e^{−r(T−t₁)}, t₁). That the chooser-date values are conditional expectations of the maturity payoffs is assumed, not derived.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.ChooserComposition

open MeasureTheory
open MathFin

/-- **Rubinstein's chooser formula as an expected payoff.** Re-exports
`MathFin.chooser_price_eq_expected_payoff`. -/
theorem chooser_price_bs {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {Q : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {S_0 K r σ T t_1 : ℝ} {Z : Ω → ℝ}
    (h : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K r σ t_1 Z) (ht : t_1 < T) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (-r * t_1) * max (bsV K r σ (bsTerminal S_0 r σ t_1 (Z ω)) (T - t_1))
        (bsP K r σ (bsTerminal S_0 r σ t_1 (Z ω)) (T - t_1)) ∂Q
      = chooserPrice S_0 K r σ T t_1 :=
  MathFin.chooser_price_eq_expected_payoff h ht

metadata.reference: M. Rubinstein, Options for the undecided, Risk 4(4) (1991) 43
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.chooser_price_eq_expected_payoff (MathFin/BlackScholes/ChooserComposition.lean): put–call parity at t₁, bs_put_formula, and integral_discounted_bsV_at_date (the discounted call price averaged over the lognormal law of S_{t₁} via integral_bsV_mul_exp_gaussianReal_of_sq). SCOPE: the chooser-date option values are taken to be the Black–Scholes price functions of S_{t₁}; the conditional-expectation (Markov) step is not re-derived.

theorems.name: Heynen–Kat Two-Asset Barrier at Zero Correlation
theorems.description: Reduced core: proves that the transcribed Heynen–Kat closed form for a call on asset 1 knocked out by asset 2, at correlation 0 and cost of carry b₁ = r, equals the Black–Scholes call bsV on asset 1 times the closed-form barrier factor Φ(φe₁) − e^{2μ₂log(H/S₂)/σ₂²}Φ(φe₃) of asset 2. The Heynen–Kat formula is not derived as a discounted expected payoff, and the barrier factor's reflection-principle reading is not proved.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.HeynenKatTwoAssetBarrier

open MathFin

/-- **Heynen–Kat at ρ = 0: Black–Scholes call times barrier factor.** Re-exports
`MathFin.heynenKatA_call_rho_zero_eq_bsV`. -/
theorem heynen_kat_independent_call (phi S1 S2 X H T r b2 σ1 σ2 : ℝ) :
    heynenKatA 1 phi S1 S2 X H T r r b2 σ1 σ2 0 =
      bsV X r σ1 S1 T *
        (Phi (phi * hkE1 H S2 b2 σ1 σ2 0 T) -
          Real.exp (2 * hkMu b2 σ2 * Real.log (H / S2) / σ2 ^ 2) *
            Phi (phi * hkE3 H S2 b2 σ1 σ2 0 T)) :=
  MathFin.heynenKatA_call_rho_zero_eq_bsV phi S1 S2 X H T r b2 σ1 σ2

metadata.reference: R. Heynen and H. Kat, Crossing barriers, Risk 7(6) (1994) 46–51
metadata.formalization_scope: Reduced core. Re-export of MathFin.heynenKatA_call_rho_zero_eq_bsV (MathFin/BlackScholes/HeynenKatTwoAssetBarrier.lean): heynenKatA_rho_zero plus hkD1 = bsd1, hkD2 = bsd2 at b₁ = r. SCOPE: an identity between closed forms at ρ = 0 and b₁ = r. NOT PROVED: that heynenKatA is the discounted expected knock-out payoff (needs the joint law of one GBM and the running extremum of a second), and the probabilistic reading of the barrier factor.

theorems.name: Kirk's Spread Approximation Is Exact at Zero Strike
theorems.description: For two Black–Scholes terminal prices driven by a jointly Gaussian pair of standard normals with correlation ρ and a non-degenerate spread variance σ₁² + σ₂² − 2ρσ₁σ₂ > 0, Kirk's approximate spread-option price at strike K = 0 equals the discounted expected spread payoff E[e^{−rT}·max(S¹_T − S²_T − 0, 0)]. No accuracy statement is made for K ≠ 0.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.KirkSpreadApproximation

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin

/-- **Kirk at zero strike is the expected spread payoff.** Re-exports
`MathFin.kirkSpreadPrice_zero_eq_expected`. -/
theorem kirk_zero_strike_expected {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {W₁ W₂ : Ω → ℝ} {σ1 σ2 ρ S1 S2 r T : ℝ}
    (hjoint : HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (W₁ ω, W₂ ω)) P)
    (hW₁meas : Measurable W₁) (hW₂meas : Measurable W₂)
    (hW₁ : HasLaw W₁ (gaussianReal 0 1) P) (hW₂ : HasLaw W₂ (gaussianReal 0 1) P)
    (hcov : cov[W₁, W₂; P] = ρ) (hS1 : 0 < S1) (hS2 : 0 < S2) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hv : 0 < σ1 ^ 2 + σ2 ^ 2 - 2 * ρ * σ1 * σ2) :
    kirkSpreadPrice S1 S2 0 r σ1 σ2 ρ T
      = ∫ ω, Real.exp (-(r * T)) *
          max (bsTerminal S1 r σ1 T (W₁ ω) - bsTerminal S2 r σ2 T (W₂ ω) - 0) 0 ∂P :=
  MathFin.kirkSpreadPrice_zero_eq_expected hjoint hW₁meas hW₂meas hW₁ hW₂ hcov hS1 hS2 hT hv

theorems.name: Stulz's Call on the Maximum at Zero Strike
theorems.description: Reduced core: proves that, for two Black–Scholes terminal prices driven by a jointly Gaussian pair of standard normals with correlation ρ (σ₁, σ₂, T > 0, non-degenerate spread variance) and equal costs of carry b₁ = b₂ = r, Stulz's transcribed closed form for a call on max(S¹, S²) tends, as the strike K ↓ 0, to the discounted expected better-of-two payoff E[e^{−rT}·max(S¹_T, S²_T)] = S²₀ + Margrabe. Stulz's formula for K > 0 is not derived as a discounted expected payoff, and its correlation parameters ρ₁, ρ₂ are not checked by this limit.

theorems.name: Margrabe's Exchange-Option Formula
theorems.description: For two Black–Scholes terminal prices S^i_T = S^i_0·exp((r − σ_i²/2)T + σ_i√T·W_i) driven by a jointly Gaussian pair of standard normals with correlation ρ, and σ_eff > 0 with σ_eff² = σ₁² + σ₂² − 2ρσ₁σ₂, the discounted expected exchange payoff E[e^{−rT}·max(S¹_T − S²_T, 0)] equals Margrabe's price S¹₀Φ(d₁) − S²₀Φ(d₂).

open MathFin

`MathFin.margrabe_exchange_price`. -/
theorem margrabe_exchange_expected {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {W₁ W₂ : Ω → ℝ} {σ₁ σ₂ ρ σeff S1 S2 r T : ℝ}
    (hjoint : HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (W₁ ω, W₂ ω)) P)
    (hW₁meas : Measurable W₁) (hW₂meas : Measurable W₂)
    (hW₁ : HasLaw W₁ (gaussianReal 0 1) P) (hW₂ : HasLaw W₂ (gaussianReal 0 1) P)
    (hcov : cov[W₁, W₂; P] = ρ)

    (hσeff_sq : σeff ^ 2 = σ₁ ^ 2 + σ₂ ^ 2 - 2 * ρ * σ₁ * σ₂) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (-(r * T)) *
        max (bsTerminal S1 r σ₁ T (W₁ ω) - bsTerminal S2 r σ₂ T (W₂ ω)) 0 ∂P
      = margrabePrice S1 S2 σeff T :=
  MathFin.margrabe_exchange_price hjoint hW₁meas hW₂meas hW₁ hW₂ hcov hS1 hS2 hσeff hT hσeff_sq

theorems.name: The Better-of-Two Option: the Second Asset plus Margrabe
theorems.description: For two Black–Scholes terminal prices S^i_T = S^i_0·exp((r − σ_i²/2)T + σ_i√T·W_i) driven by a jointly Gaussian pair of standard normals with correlation ρ, σ₂ > 0, and σ_eff > 0 with σ_eff² = σ₁² + σ₂² − 2ρσ₁σ₂, the discounted expected better-of-two payoff E[e^{−rT}·max(S¹_T, S²_T)] equals S²₀ plus Margrabe's exchange price: the rainbow option on the maximum at zero strike. theorems.name: Partial-Time Barrier: Down-Window Plus Up-Window
theorems.description: Proves that, for Haug's partial-time (start-window, call) barrier closed form CA, summing the down-window (eta=1) and up-window (eta=-1) values collapses every bivariate normal CDF term to a single univariate Phi, via bivariateNormalCDF_flip_snd, whose hypothesis rho^2 <= 1 holds whenever the monitoring window [0,t1] is a sub-interval of the option's life [0,T].

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.PartialTimeBarrierOption

open MathFin

/-- **Down-window plus up-window, same strike/barrier.** Re-exports
`MathFin.ptCA_down_add_up`. -/
theorem partial_time_barrier_down_add_up (S X H b r σ t1 T : ℝ) (ht1 : 0 ≤ t1) (hT : t1 ≤ T) :
    ptCA 1 S X H b r σ t1 T + ptCA (-1) S X H b r σ t1 T
      = S * Real.exp ((b - r) * T) *
          (Phi (ptD1 S X b σ T) - ptHSmu1 S H b σ * Phi (ptF1 S X H b σ T))
        - X * Real.exp (-r * T) *
            (Phi (ptD2 S X b σ T) - ptHSmu S H b σ * Phi (ptF2 S X H b σ T)) :=
  MathFin.ptCA_down_add_up S X H b r σ t1 T ht1 hT

metadata.reference: Haug, The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas, §"Partial-Time Barrier Options"

The Haug/Heynen–Kat start-window closed form is transcribed, not derived: what is proved is (1) the in–out collapse CA(1) + CA(−1) to the t₁-free full-life down-and-out expression, via bivariateNormalCDF_flip_snd, and (2) the whole-life reduction — at t₁ = T (X ≥ H) the correlation is 1 and bivariateNormalCDF_one turns ptCA into that same standard-barrier closed form. The barrier density itself (the reflection-principle step behind the transcribed N₂ terms) is not proved; main's precedent for transcribed barriers proving no more than this is reduced_core (Heynen–Kat, Stulz). Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Binary Barrier In-Out Parity (Down and Up Families)
